title: The Snowman

full_text:
"It crackles so delightfully within me!" said the Snowman, gazing with coal-black eyes across the snowy yard. "The biting frost is delicious! But tell me, old watchdog, what is that bright, glowing thing peering through the cellar window?"

"That is the stove!" barked the watchdog. "It radiates glowing heat and cooks delicious bone broth! Keep your distance, Snowman, or it will melt you to water!"

The Snowman could not tear his eyes from the cellar window. Through the glass, he saw the stove glowing with fiery embers, sending warm red light dancing across the floor. An irresistible, agonizing longing filled his snowy chest: "Oh, to be near that glowing stove! To feel that warmth, even if it melts me!"

All night, through freezing starlight, the Snowman stood watching the stove, his heart burning with cold passion.

When morning dawned, the south wind blew softly; the thaw set in. As the golden sun climbed the sky, the Snowman began to melt. Down he dripped into a pool of water upon the flagstones.

When he was gone, the watchdog saw what had been in the center of the Snowman: a long iron stove scraper around which the boys had molded his snowy body!

"Ah!" barked the watchdog. "Now I understand why he longed so passionately for the stove—he had a stove scraper in his body! It was in his very blood!"
moral: Yearning for what warms the heart can bring dissolution, yet longing is the essence of being alive.
